chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih and Al-Nawfali, and others, with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not treat himself for catarrh (runny nose), and he would say: 'There is no one but that he has a vein of leprosy in him; so if catarrh strikes him, it suppresses it.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) not treat his runny nose according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Prophet’s (SAW) practice of allowing minor ailments like catarrh to persist, interpreting them as a natural purgation of the 'vein of leprosy' inherent in every human. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of *tadawi* (healing) as a balance between seeking medical remedy and accepting divine decree, where minor afflictions serve as expiation for sins or physical cleansing. The hadith underscores the Prophetic model of moderation in health, avoiding excessive intervention for transient conditions.

en.hubeali: H 15024 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Bakr bin Salih, and Al-Nowfali, and someone else with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdullahasws, the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said:

‘The Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> never used to cure himself<sup>saww</sup> from the flu, and would say: ‘There is no one except that he has a vein from the leprosy, so if he is struck by the flu, it suppresses it’.
en.sarwar: 578. Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, who has narrated the following: ‘Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said;
‘The Rasool Allah (saww) said: ‘The flu is an army from the armies of Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic. Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic Sends it to the illness, to eradicate it’.
